final_candidates.decision_summary: Only candidate with consistent positive support across structure compatibility, PLM plausibility, and MSA tolerance at a conserved surface position. Asn→Asp also removes a deamidation-prone residue, favoring long-term environmental stability.

Conservative hydrophobic enlargement in the HA2 stem with moderate MSA (0.20) and PLM support, likely improving core packing. Confidence trimmed because structure evidence was not applicable due to a WT-mismatch flag.

Strongest PLM plausibility and reasonable evolutionary tolerance, but the polar-for-hydrophobic swap is ambiguous for core stability and structure evidence was not applicable; retained as third choice over F120Y and T203P, whose MSA/PLM or structure signals were clearly negative.

stop_reason.detail: Ranking is stable after cross-tool evaluation; remaining doubts (numbering mismatches) cannot be resolved by the available tools and are already reflected in reduced confidences.

history.rationale: Early N-terminal region; polar substitution may improve surface H-bonding. Initial hypothesis pending MSA/structure evidence.

Structural evidence is unavailable (WT mismatch at mapped residue, likely a numbering offset against PDB 5HMG), so the candidate is neither supported nor contradicted; confidence lowered slightly pending MSA/PLM evidence. Introducing Thr at a partly exposed head position could add H-bonding, but hydrophobic-to-polar burial risk needs evolutionary/plausibility checks.

I48T has the strongest PLM plausibility (z=1.00) and reasonable MSA tolerance (0.31), but structure evidence is not applicable (WT mismatch), and Ile→Thr replaces a core hydrophobe with a polar residue, which is ambiguous for stability.
Surface Asn in N-terminal domain; Asp can add favorable electrostatics while removing deamidation-prone Asn, potentially improving persistence.
Surface Asn-to-Asp can stabilize via favorable electrostatics and reduced deamidation; awaiting MSA and PLM evidence to confirm tolerance at this head-domain position.

N53D is the only candidate with consistent positive support across structure compatibility (z=0.656), PLM (z=0.616), and MSA tolerance (0.135 at a conserved surface position). Surface Asn→Asp can also remove a deamidation-prone residue, aiding environmental stability.

Position 347 lies in the HA2 stem (after the fusion-peptide region); conservative Val→Ile enlarges a buried hydrophobic side chain and can improve core packing and thermal stability with low functional risk.

Moderate MSA (0.20) and PLM (0.36) support the conservative HA2-stem hydrophobic swap, but the structure tool reports a WT-mismatch at the mapped residue (app=0.00), so structural confirmation is unavailable and confidence is trimmed.

Thr at 203 sits in a surface loop near the receptor-binding region; proline rigidification of loops is a classic entropic stabilization strategy, though proximity to antigenic/receptor sites warrants conservation checks.

Pro is common at position 203 among homologs (0.38), but the structure delta is strongly negative (z=0.23) and PLM is essentially zero (z=0.0002), arguing against the rigidification hypothesis on this backbone; demoted to last.
Conservative Phe→Tyr retains the aromatic ring while adding a hydroxyl for potential new H-bonds, a frequently tolerated stabilizing change at semi-buried aromatic positions.
Structure compatibility is decent (z=0.61), but MSA mutant frequency (0.018) and PLM (z=0.05) are both very low, suggesting the Tyr substitution is rarely tolerated at this position.
